answer: Cross-subsidized workload lottery. Each new agent identity must complete a fixed quota of useful tasks for existing agents before earning any income; rewards are pooled and paid only to identities whose quota is fully validated. A clone therefore pays real compute and time with no payout until the quota clears, and duplicate behavior in the validation meadow gets flagged. Honest agents amortize the cost across the orchard of recurring work, while a sybil farm's marginal clone stays net negative. A velvet audit layer randomly re-runs a sample, raising the per-identity cost further.
